item.title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
item.description: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

item.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
item.description: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
item.description: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
item.description: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.

item.title: Dems have edge in midterms, poll shows. And, Paramount-Warner Bros. merger to close
item.description: Polls are showing that Democrats have a clear advantage heading into the midterms, but that doesn't tell the whole story. And, today, a mega merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. is set to close.

item.title: A history of presidents naming things after themselves (It's short. They rarely do)
item.description: While Trump pushes to get his name on the Kennedy Center and other public sites, history shows that sitting presidents have almost always avoided putting their brands on government assets.

item.description: Democrats are feeling optimistic ahead of the midterms, but what challenges remain? NPR's A Martinez asks Devan Barber, who leads the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.

item.title: Disney, ABC battle Trump's FCC in court over free speech protections
item.description: President Trump has repeatedly called for Disney's ABC to fire late night comedian Jimmy Kimmel, for mocking him. Trump has also routinely denounced ABC's The View, accusing it of being unfair.
